newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli Arab lawmaker wants bedouin to quit army.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Arab lawmaker wants bedouin to quit army.

text.p: An Israeli Arab legislator has called for bedouin to stop serving in the army of the Jewish state.
"In light of its (the current government's) warlikeness...we are calling on the bedouin soldiers to turn in their draft cards," Taleb al-Sana, himself a bedouin, told Reuters on Tuesday.

Sana, of the Arab Democratic Party, said it was his longstanding position that Arabs of any stripe should work for peace and not bear arms for Israel but he was issuing a special call now because of the government.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ousted the previous centre-right government -- that cut interim peace deals with the Palestinians and a peace treaty with Jordan -- in May elections.
Netanyahu rejects trading occupied Arab land for peace, key to the peace negotiations conducted by the previous government.
There are some 750,000 non-Jews in Israel's 5.7 million population, of those a small percentage are bedouin, some of whom volunteer to serve in the Israeli army.
Of the non-Jews, only Israeli Druze must serve in the army, an Israeli army spokeswoman said.
